data.protocol: Use the same fitted log-linear allometry log(volume)=intercept+bD*log(diameter)+bH*log(height) for both reports. Logs are natural and use the numeric source units. Fit only the21 training trees. Compare naive exp(predictedlog) with training-residual smearing: multiply exp(predictedlog) by the arithmetic mean of exp(log(observed training volume)-predicted training log volume). Do not estimate that factor from test residuals or refit on test trees. Compare RMSE on original ft3 test volumes; keep all ties within1e-9. Pooled smearing has a mean-oriented interpretation under a shared residual distribution; it is not proof of unbiasedness under heteroscedasticity, or a carbon conversion.
data.unit_dictionary: Original R Girth is actually diameter in inches, not circumference. Height is feet; recorded timber volume is ft3. No unit conversion is needed because fitted intercept accommodates these declared source units.
data.panel_derivation: Unchanged31 measured trees; default_rng(212).permutation(31), first21train and remaining10test. Source tree IDs are one-based original R positions. No synthetic measurements or response edits.
